body.en: *Bacteria* are the sole members of Monera and are the most abundant micro-organisms. By shape they are coccus (spherical), bacillus (rod-shaped), vibrio (comma-shaped) and spirillum (spiral).

say.en: Bacteria come in four shapes.
Coccus is round, bacillus a rod, vibrio a comma and spirillum a spiral.
Archaebacteria live in extreme places: salty, hot and marshy.
Cyanobacteria like Nostoc are filaments; the large heterocyst fixes nitrogen.
Mycoplasma has no cell wall at all and is the smallest living cell.
On the board: Kingdom Monera.

body.en: *Archaebacteria* live in extreme habitats: halophiles in salty areas, thermoacidophiles in hot springs and methanogens in marshy areas. Their cell wall structure is different from other bacteria. Methanogens live in the gut of ruminants such as cows and buffaloes and produce methane (biogas) from their dung.
body.kn: ಆರ್ಕಿಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾ ಕಠಿಣ ಪರಿಸರಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಬದುಕುತ್ತವೆ: ಹ್ಯಾಲೋಫೈಲ್‌ಗಳು ಉಪ್ಪಿನಲ್ಲಿ, ಥರ್ಮೋಆಸಿಡೋಫೈಲ್‌ಗಳು ಬಿಸಿನೀರಿನ ಬುಗ್ಗೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ, ಮೆಥನೋಜೆನ್‌ಗಳು ಮೆಲುಕು ಹಾಕುವ ಪ್ರಾಣಿಗಳ ಕರುಳಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಮೀಥೇನ್ ಉತ್ಪಾದಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: *Eubacteria* have a rigid cell wall and, if motile, a flagellum. Cyanobacteria have chlorophyll a and some, like Nostoc and Anabaena, fix nitrogen in heterocysts. Chemosynthetic bacteria oxidise inorganic substances such as nitrates and ammonia for energy. Heterotrophic bacteria are decomposers, make curd and antibiotics, and cause diseases like cholera, typhoid, tetanus and citrus canker. Mycoplasma has no cell wall at all and is the smallest living cell.
body.kn: ಯೂಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾಗಳಿಗೆ ಗಟ್ಟಿ ಕೋಶಭಿತ್ತಿ ಇದೆ. ನಾಸ್ಟಾಕ್, ಅನಾಬೀನಾದ ಹೆಟೆರೋಸಿಸ್ಟ್‌ಗಳು ಸಾರಜನಕ ಸ್ಥಿರೀಕರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಮೈಕೋಪ್ಲಾಸ್ಮಾಗೆ ಕೋಶಭಿತ್ತಿ ಇಲ್ಲ; ಅದು ಅತಿ ಚಿಕ್ಕ ಜೀವಕೋಶ.

say.en: Bacteria are the most abundant micro-organisms and live almost everywhere: hot springs, deserts, snow, deep oceans, inside other organisms. By shape they are coccus (spherical), bacillus (rod), vibrio (comma) and spirillum (spiral).

Habitat: archaebacteria in extremes (salt pans of Rann of Kutch, hot springs of Manikaran); eubacteria everywhere. Cell wall: archaebacteria have a chemically different wall (no peptidoglycan); eubacteria have a rigid peptidoglycan wall.

problem.en: A biogas plant in a village uses cattle dung. Which organisms make the gas, what kind of Monera are they, and where do they come from?

steps.en: The gas is mainly methane, made by methanogens.
Methanogens are archaebacteria, which live in anaerobic, marshy conditions.
They live in the gut of ruminants like cows and buffaloes and come out with the dung.

Pause and solve this exam pattern question. Which of the following were criteria used by R.H. Whittaker for his five-kingdom classification?
i Cell structure
ii Mode of nutrition
iii Chromosome number
iv Phylogenetic relationships.
Whittaker used cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships.
Chromosome number was not one of his criteria.

narration.en: Recap. Bacteria: coccus, bacillus, vibrio, spirillum. Archaebacteria live in extreme habitats; methanogens make biogas. Nostoc and Anabaena fix nitrogen in heterocysts. Mycoplasma lacks a cell wall and is the smallest living cell.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾ ಆಕಾರಗಳು: ಕಾಕಸ್, ಬ್ಯಾಸಿಲಸ್, ವಿಬ್ರಿಯೊ, ಸ್ಪೈರಿಲಮ್. ಆರ್ಕಿಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾ ಕಠಿಣ ಪರಿಸರದಲ್ಲಿ; ಮೆಥನೋಜೆನ್‌ಗಳು ಜೈವಿಕ ಅನಿಲ ತಯಾರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ನಾಸ್ಟಾಕ್, ಅನಾಬೀನಾ ಹೆಟೆರೋಸಿಸ್ಟ್‌ಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಾರಜನಕ ಸ್ಥಿರೀಕರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಮೈಕೋಪ್ಲಾಸ್ಮಾಗೆ ಕೋಶಭಿತ್ತಿ ಇಲ್ಲ; ಅದು ಅತಿ ಚಿಕ್ಕ ಜೀವಕೋಶ.
